text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening stance and repeated claim that driverless cars are unsafe","quality":"position clarity","description":"This captures how explicitly and consistently the essay states its argument and stays on that side throughout."},{"evidence":"“what if that technology gets destroyed?” “what if it just stops completely?”","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"This captures how the essay raises specific failure scenarios to make its case against driverless cars."},{"evidence":"driver, lanes, potholes, stop sign, little boy crossing the street","quality":"concrete support","description":"This captures the use of vivid, specific examples to illustrate why human drivers may be safer in real situations."},{"evidence":"technology freezes / who is at fault-the driver or the manufacturer?","quality":"source integration","description":"This captures how the essay directly uses and responds to a detail from the article as evidence for its argument."},{"evidence":"driver might fall asleep or get distracted while the car is doing all the work","quality":"cause-effect reasoning","description":"This captures the essay’s attempt to explain how driverless technology could lead to worse driver attention and therefore more danger."},{"evidence":"intro body and conclusion with repeated closing question","quality":"overall organization","description":"This captures the essay’s clearer essay structure, with a beginning, development of reasons, and a concluding wrap-up."}]}
